newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR says sugar crushing season going well.
newsitem.headline: CSR says sugar crushing season going well.

text.p: Building products, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd said on Monday the 1997 season sugar crop in its mill areas was likely to be a record and that the crushing season is going well.
CSR chairman Alan Coates told the annual general meeting that capital expenditure to cope with increased sugar cane production over the past few years had amounted to A$400 million.
Capacity had increased 55 percent and the expansion programme in CSR's sugar mills was nearing completion.

"The forecast raw sugar price for this season is lower than for last season but, with increased throughput in Queensland and improved performance from the Ord River mill, the profits from raw sugar should be similar to last year," Coates said.
"There is some prospect of modest improvement if the current world raw sugar price level holds and the Australian dollar remains at the present value against the U.S. dollar," he said.
CSR reported a lower net profit of A$53.60 million for the year to March 31, 1996 from its sugar operations, down from A$64.70 million the previous year.
Coates said further viable expansion in CSR's milling capacity would depend on the company arriving at a satisfactory supply agreement with growers including a longer crushing season.
Negotiations had commenced on this matter in the Burdekin and Herbert districts.
"In refined sugar the gross over-capacity in Australia has led to a price war which threatens the viability of the industry," Coates said.
"It is our hope that the removal of the tariff on sugar imports will be the catalyst for a restructuring of the industry," he said.
The Australian government announced in March that it would abolish the A$55 a tonne tariff on imported raw and refined sugar from July 1, 1997.
